selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent multi-hop exploration and interaction sequence. The player must first locate gravel and smooth_sandstone_slab as navigation landmarks that guide them toward the gold_ore deposit. Mining gold_ore requires finding it first, which is facilitated by navigating past the gravel and sandstone landmarks. Finally, renaming a helmet requires the player to have located an anvil (placed near the gold_ore area), creating a natural progression from exploration to mining to item manipulation. The dependency structure creates a diamond-shaped DAG where two parallel exploration tasks converge on mining, which then leads to the final renaming task.

edges.reason: Gravel patch is placed along the path leading to the gold_ore deposit, serving as a navigation waypoint
Smooth sandstone slab structure marks the entrance to the mining area containing gold_ore
The anvil for renaming is located in the same underground area as the gold_ore, discovered after mining

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The gravel patch is a 4x3 area at spawn-relative (4,-1,3) to (7,-1,5), centered around (5,0,4). Max distance reduced to 8 from 16 to prevent trivial satisfaction from spawn position, ensuring the player intentionally navigated toward the gravel.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The smooth sandstone slabs are a 3x2 area at spawn-relative (-5,0,6) to (-3,0,7), centered around (-4,0,7). Max distance reduced to 8 to ensure intentional navigation rather than accidental proximity from spawn.

Uses inventory_has because mining gold ore with an iron pickaxe drops raw_gold into the player's inventory. The player starts with 0 raw_gold, so having at least 1 confirms successful mining. This is the strongest mechanical verification — directly checks the mining outcome.

Uses position_near_with_facing targeting the anvil at spawn-relative (7,0,10) with max_distance=3 (within Minecraft's block interaction range of ~4.5 blocks). This is the best verifiable proxy for the rename action because the evaluation system's info dict cannot detect custom item names — inventory only exposes type and quantity. The tight distance (3 blocks) ensures the player is close enough to actually interact with the anvil. Scene provides 30 XP levels to make the rename mechanically possible.

scene_description: An open grass field with distinct landmarks: a gravel patch to the right-forward area, smooth sandstone slabs to the left-forward area, a gold ore deposit in the far-right corner with an anvil nearby. The player spawns with an iron pickaxe, iron helmet, and 30 XP levels. The layout supports sequential exploration (find gravel and sandstone slabs as waypoints), mining (gold ore with iron pickaxe), and item manipulation (rename helmet at anvil).
task_text: Explore the area to find a gravel patch and smooth sandstone slabs as landmarks. Then locate and mine gold ore using your iron pickaxe. Finally, find the anvil and rename your iron helmet.
design_notes: Layout: Player spawns at origin (0,0,0). Gravel patch is 4x3 blocks at (~4-7, -1, ~3-5). Smooth sandstone slabs are 3x2 at (~-5 to -3, 0, ~6-7). Gold ore cluster (2x2 exposed at y=0, plus 2 underground at y=-1) at (~8-9, 0, ~8-9). Anvil at (~7, 0, ~10). Player has iron pickaxe (mining level 2, sufficient for gold ore), iron helmet (to rename), and 30 XP levels (covers anvil rename cost). No name tag needed — item renaming on anvil only requires the item + XP.
